annotationRationale: Two applications of the Pythagorean theorem and a square-of-a-sum identity determine the diagonal. Prism edge and face structure supplies the needed symmetric sums. The supplied explanations support one substantive route.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The edge and face totals give a+b+c=13/4 and ab+bc+ca=11/4, hence the body diagonal is sqrt(81/16)=9/4, choice D. Distinct lengths 1/4, 1, and 2 also satisfy the volume condition, so the data are consistent. All body diagonals have equal length. No figure or choice contradiction.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2023_AMC_10B_Q17 / find-squared-diagonal-from-totals was independently checked against this identical problem and retained. LIVE and Random Math use the equivalent identity route. Solving for the individual lengths would add unnecessary work.
review.annotationCheck: Pythagorean theorem and multiplication-formula application are appropriately assessed; prism structure and surface area are appropriate support. Replacing the previous spatial-coordinate-distance emphasis matches the actual derivation.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Four edges of each length and two faces of each area give the stated symmetric sums. Two justified right triangles yield AC²=a²+b²+c². Subtracting 2(ab+bc+ca) from (a+b+c)² gives (169-88)/16=81/16, so the positive diagonal length is 9/4. The unused volume creates no conflict.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The exact shared question and method are credited. Both inherited IDs, live-reference-2023_AMC_10B_Q17 and randommath-reference-2023_AMC_10B_Q17, are retained alongside the shared reference and current references. Reuse matches the supplied methodLocalSources provenance. Source-informed-original correctly distinguishes project prose and third-party evidence from an official MAA argument.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why symmetric sums are useful. The verbal vertex construction fully justifies the spatial diagonal formula, and the algebra is reconstructible without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_174 directly covers both right-triangle applications. cnm_149 covers combining and evaluating the multiplication identity. Neither a coordinate-distance node nor a separate node for the derived body-diagonal formula is necessary.
